title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages). S is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue field h. U/K is a hyperbolic curve of type (g,ν). π = π_1(U_η̄) is its geometric fundamental group, T ⊂ Gal(K̄/K) is the inertia group, and E_h = Gal(h̄/h). Sequence (30) is presumably 1→T→Gal(K̄/K)→E_h→1, and (31) is 1→π→π_1(U)→Gal(K̄/K)→1.

The page continues the 'Conjecture-à-tout-hasard': the following conditions should be equivalent.
(a) U has good reduction over S.
(b) The outer action of T on π is trivial. Equivalently, any splitting of (31), e.g. one coming from a K-rational point of U, restricted to T gives a homomorphism T→π.
(c) T acts trivially on π^ab = H_1(U_η̄).
(d) The same for H_1(U_η̄, Z_ℓ) (the transcription's 'T_ℓ' is probably Z_ℓ), with ℓ prime to the residue characteristic. NB: for ℓ = p > 0 the condition should be expressible through p-divisible groups.
(e) Now take h of finite type over Q, so S is in equal characteristic 0 and T ≅ Ẑ(1). A section of (30), pulled back through (31), gives an extension of E_h by π, i.e. an outer action of E_h on π. Condition: this extension is 'admissible', meaning it comes from an algebraic curve over h or over a finite extension of h.
(f) Sections of both (30) and (31) give a genuine action of E_h on π. Condition: this action 'is not too crazy' (pas trop loufoque), a notion still to be defined.

On the next page Grothendieck says (a)⇒(b)⇒(c)⇒(d) is evident and (d)⇒(a) should be more or less known. He adds that (a)–(d) imply (e), but he has no idea how to prove (e)⇒(a). He extracts a 'principle': curves with bad reduction should produce non-geometric outer actions of Galois groups of fields of finite type over Q on fundamental groups π of curves. These come from the 'boundary' (∞) of the Teichmüller/moduli tower, i.e. from tangential base points at infinity.

Purpose: to find a group-theoretic characterisation of geometric Galois actions on π. This is the anabelian programme of the Longue Marche and Esquisse. Here he tests it against degeneration.
errors: (d)⇒(a), and already (c)⇒(a), are false for g ≥ 2. Triviality of inertia on H_1 (Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich/Serre–Tate) gives only good reduction of the Jacobian. A curve can have bad stable reduction (e.g. a compact-type tree of components) while its Jacobian has good reduction. The correct statement needs the non-abelian π, i.e. (b)⇔(a); this is Oda's theorem.

(a)⇒(b) is too strong as stated if π is the full profinite group and the residue characteristic is p > 0. Good reduction only forces the inertia action on the prime-to-p (or pro-ℓ, ℓ≠p) quotient to be trivial. Wild inertia still acts nontrivially through Artin–Schreier-type covers. Grothendieck's own caveat in (d) points in this direction.

For ν > 0 the cusps must also be included in the good-reduction notion: the marked points must stay distinct mod the maximal ideal. Otherwise the abelian conditions fail even more clearly. The page does not make this explicit.
In (e), 'admissible' and the dependence on the chosen section of (30) are left vague. Different sections differ by elements of T, which act nontrivially in the bad-reduction case.

ideas.what: Good reduction of a hyperbolic curve should be equivalent to the outer inertia action on its (pro-ℓ) geometric fundamental group being trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Oda's criterion for good reduction (non-abelian Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich); extended to affine hyperbolic curves by Tamagawa
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted in Longue Marche-related material; not known in a published Grothendieck text

ideas.what: The abelian condition (inertia trivial on H_1 / Tate module) as a criterion for good reduction.
ideas.modern_name: Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich / Serre–Tate criterion (for the Jacobian only)
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 (Grothendieck's treatment of semistable reduction of abelian varieties)

ideas.what: For ℓ = p, the good-reduction criterion should be expressed through p-divisible groups.
ideas.modern_name: p-adic criteria for good reduction (Fontaine/Coleman–Iovita crystalline criterion; non-abelian version by Andreatta–Iovita–Kim)

ideas.what: Using a section of 1→T→G_K→G_h→1 (a tangential/‘boundary’ splitting) to turn a degenerating curve over h((t)) into an outer action of G_h on π. Conjecture: this action is geometric (comes from a curve over a finite extension of h) iff the reduction is good.
ideas.modern_name: Galois actions at tangential base points at infinity of M_{g,ν}; geometricity of outer Galois representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara–Nakamura (1997, degeneration of maximally degenerate marked curves); Nakamura; Hoshi–Mochizuki (combinatorial anabelian geometry, nodally nondegenerate outer representations)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tangential base points and the Teichmüller tower, but not this specific conjecture as far as I know

ideas.what: Principle: degenerate curves should produce non-geometric outer actions of G_k (k of finite type over Q) on surface groups.
ideas.modern_name: Non-geometric outer Galois representations / failure of a 'Hom-type' converse in anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure (related work by Hoshi and others on non-geometric pro-p objects)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, before Oda, the conjecture that good reduction of a hyperbolic curve is equivalent to trivial outer inertia action on its geometric fundamental group. This is condition (b), essentially Oda's later theorem (with Tamagawa's extension to affine curves). Grothendieck mislumps it with the abelian conditions (c),(d), which are genuinely weaker.
missed.quote: b) L'action extérieure de T sur π est triviale ... c) L'action de T sur π_ab = H_1(U_η̄) est triviale.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: the non-abelian good-reduction criterion appears in Grothendieck's Longue Marche notes, probably early 1980s, well before Oda (1990). The page also shows that the gap between (b) and (c) — that π detects more than the Jacobian — was not yet recognised by him.

missed.claim: Conjecture (e)⇒(a), in equal characteristic 0 with residue field of finite type over Q: the outer G_h-action on π obtained from a degenerating curve via a splitting of inertia is geometric only if the reduction is good. In bad reduction it gives non-geometric actions. Grothendieck leaves this unproved and admits lacking the arithmetic understanding.
missed.quote: La dite extension est admissible ... i.e. peut être défini par une courbe alg. sur k, ou sur une extension finie de k.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could now be attacked with Mochizuki's Hom-version of the Grothendieck conjecture and combinatorial anabelian geometry (Hoshi–Mochizuki). Through the structure of graphs of profinite groups, it would yield explicit non-geometric outer Galois representations coming from the boundary of M_{g,ν}. I do not know of a statement of exactly this conjecture in the literature.

missed.claim: A link between p-divisible groups (ℓ = p) and the anabelian good-reduction criterion. This anticipates p-adic non-abelian criteria such as Andreatta–Iovita–Kim.
missed.quote: ℓ = p > 0 on doit pouvoir l'exprimer par un critère sur les groupes p-divisibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest; the p-adic non-abelian criterion was later realised via unipotent crystalline fundamental groups rather than p-divisible groups.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an early, unpublished formulation of what became Oda's non-abelian good-reduction criterion. It also contains a conjecture that degenerate curves yield non-geometric Galois actions, tied to the 'infinity' of the Teichmüller tower. Its abelian part contains a genuine error, so the content is notable historically, but the core (b)⇔(a) is now a known theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'H_1(U_η̄, T_ℓ)' is likely H_1(U_η̄, Z_ℓ) (ℓ-adic homology).
In e), 'Etant donnés deux sections de (30)' should read 'Etant donnée une section de (30)'.
In f), 'cette actions n'est pas trop loufoque' should read 'cette action n'est pas trop loufoque (à définir convenablement !)'.
The inserted '(ou un)' in the first line refers to 'un scindage de (31)'; 'pt de U_η̄ rat/K' means a K-rational point of U.
